title: API keys and the JS SDK
summary: The owner creates, uses, restricts, rolls and revokes API keys in the portal; requests with the keys reach the OTA API; the SDK's smoke tests run against the local stack with the demo OTA's keys.
prerequisites: An active OTA of yours and the OTA API on port 4000.
`curl` and `jq`. For the SDK smoke tests: the four keys printed by the OTA's `dev:seed` ([[journey:run-the-stack]]).

steps.title: The API keys page
steps.expect: The **Test keys** tab lists the two keys created at set-up, *Initial test key (publishable)* and *Initial test key (secret)*, with Name, Kind, Key (`prefix…last4`), Access, Created (*at set-up*), Last used (*Never* until used), Expires and Status *Active*. No **Live keys** tab while the OTA is in test.
steps.data: `SELECT name, kind, environment, prefix, scopes, allowed_origins, last_used_at, revoked_at FROM platform.api_keys WHERE tenant_id = 'ten_…';`

steps.title: Create a secret key and see it once
steps.actions: Type **Name** `automation test`, keep *Secret key* and *Storefront*, press **Create the key**. Copy it. Reload.
steps.expect: The region **Your new secret test key** with *Copy this now: it is shown only once* and the key `sk_test_` + 40 characters; *In the list it shows as `sk_test_xxxxxx…abcd`*. After the reload the key is nowhere in the page and its last use reads *Never*.
steps.data: Only `key_hash` (HMAC with the pepper), the 14-character `prefix` and `last4` are stored; audit `api_key.created` holds the prefix, never the key.

steps.title: Call the OTA API with the key
steps.actions: Run `curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: sk_test_…' http://localhost:4000/v1/storefront | jq '.brand // .'`, then the same with a wrong key. Wait five minutes and reload the API keys page.
steps.expect: 200 with your OTA's storefront configuration; the wrong key answers `401` with the error envelope (`INVALID_API_KEY`) and an `X-Request-Id`. After the flush, *Last used* shows the time.
steps.data: Redis `apikey:<prefix>` (cached row, 60 s) and `apikey:used:<keyId>`; after the platform worker's 5-minute flush `platform.api_keys.last_used_at` is set.

steps.title: A storefront-scoped key cannot reach the console
steps.expect: `403 SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED` (the `storefront` scope is refused on every console operation).

steps.title: A publishable key restricted to one origin
steps.actions: Create a *Publishable key* with the allowed origin `http://localhost:8080`. Call `curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: pk_test_…' -H 'Origin: http://localhost:8080' http://localhost:4000/v1/storefront`, then with `Origin: http://localhost:9999`, then without `Origin`. Try saving an origin with a path or a wildcard.
steps.expect: The allowed origin answers 200; another origin `403 ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`; no `Origin` at all (a server-side call) answers 200 too: the list restricts browsers only. Invalid origins are refused by the form (an origin, no path, no wildcard; `http://localhost:<port>` only for test keys).

steps.title: Revoke a key
steps.actions: Press **Revoke** on the secret key; read the dialog; press **Revoke the key**. Repeat the curl of step "use" at once.
steps.expect: The dialog says *Requests with `<masked key>` stop working within a minute.* The row shows *Revoked* without actions. The curl answers `401` within about a second (the `api_key` invalidation; 60 s at most).

steps.title: Roll a key with an overlap
steps.actions: Roll the publishable key with an expiry of the old key in 1 hour.
steps.expect: A new key with the same name, kind, origins and scopes is shown once; the old key keeps working until its `expires_at`, then answers `401`.
steps.data: Two rows: the old with `expires_at` set, the new one active; audit `api_key.rolled`.

steps.title: Run the SDK smoke tests against the local stack
steps.actions: With the OTA API running, run `SDK_SMOKE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_… SDK_SMOKE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_… SDK_SMOKE_CONSOLE_KEY=sk_test_… pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk test:smoke` with the demo OTA's three seeded keys. `REDIS_URL` and `DATABASE_MIGRATOR_URL` come from the root `.env.local` (development values only).
steps.expect: Both files pass: token mode (storefront, reference, search and price, a guest checkout, customer sign-up, account and bookings, sign-out; the console refused with `PermissionError` `403 SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED`) and server mode (the same journey with `endUser`, the storefront key refused on the console, the console key with a staff token). Every response carries a request id. Token-mode sign-ups count against 127.0.0.1 (5 per hour), so a sixth run within an hour fails with `429`.
